2011_027_090611regmtg.paragraph: Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting held September 6, 2011 at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. Agenda business included recognition of spring 2011 All-State athletes, the MASB President's Award of Recognition to Ida Edmunds, a twenty-second consecutive ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting, and a Resolution of Respect for former board member Anthony Spagnola. The most consequential action item was a resolution committing the district to enter a Service Consolidation Plan Agreement with the Michigan Department of Education so Troy could qualify for the one-time $100 per pupil Best Financial Practices incentive payment for 2011-2012.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, September 6, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000.

**Recognition**
- Fifteen spring 2011 All-State athletes from Troy High and Athens High, among them Olivia Brannon (Athens girls soccer; Ms. Soccer, Gatorade Player of the Year, ESPN Player of the Year for MI) and Joseph Kemp (Athens boys lacrosse, All American).
- MASB President's Award of Recognition to Ida Edmunds for completing all seven levels of certification and 1,383 certification credits, presented by MASB Executive Director Kathy Hayes.
- ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the CAFR for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2010, the twenty-second year in a row, recognizing Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services.
- Resolution of Respect for Anthony Spagnola, born May 20, 1950 in Easton, Pennsylvania, died July 20, 2011 at age 61, who served on the board from July 1991 through June 2007.

**August 16, 2011 minutes (consent agenda)**
Called to order 7:24 p.m., adjourned 7:44 p.m., seven members present. Resolutions 11-081 (June and July 2011 Treasurer's Report, diesel fuel bid award), 11-082 (ten new hires), 11-083 (Section 105c, ten non-resident 10th graders for 2011-2012), 11-084 (Section 105c, unlimited 9th graders for 2012-2013) and 11-085 (MASB ballot for Donald Hubler, Region 8) each passed 7-0.

**Personnel**

**Enrollment**

An August 31, 2011 summary totals 6531 secondary students and 448 in the International Academy.

**Business and Other**
Resolution to enter a Service Consolidation Plan Agreement with the Michigan Department of Education under MCL 388.1622f(1)(c), compliant with MDE guidance of June 30, 2011, to qualify for the $100 per pupil Best Practices incentive offsetting the $470 per pupil reduction for 2011-12. Ida Edmunds, Paula Fleming and Todd Miletti were certified as delegates to the MASB 2011 Delegate Assembly on October 27, 2011.

Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of September 6, 2011, held at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices are at 4400 Livernois, telephone 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

RECOGNITION. Fifteen spring 2011 All-State athletes were honored: Olivia Brannon (Athens girls soccer; All State 2009, 2010, 2011 1st Team; Ms. Soccer; Gatorade Player of the Year; ESPN Player of the Year for MI), Kara Collins, Hope Keating, Emily Dzik, Alison Holland, Irene Young, Lynsey Mukomel and Kristin Soreide of Troy High School, and Joseph Kemp (All American), Daniel Kreza, Kevin Lining, Neal Mistry, Nick Youngerman, Marisa Kozikowski and Jenna O'Dell of Athens High School; coaches named include Tim Storch, Eric Sturgis, Brian Zawislak, Nick Stensen, Tom Calnen and Alison Atchoo. Board member Ida Edmunds received the Michigan Association of School Boards' President's Award of Recognition, the highest certification for a school board member, for completing all seven levels of certification and 1,383 certification credits, presented by MASB Executive Director Kathy Hayes; the MASB awards program dates to 1990 and aims at the achievement of 1.6 million Michigan students. For the twenty-second year in a row the district earned the Association of School Business Officials International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for its Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2010, recognizing Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services. A Resolution of Respect honored Anthony Spagnola, a 30-year Troy resident born in Easton, Pennsylvania on May 20, 1950 and departed July 20, 2011 at age 61, who served on the Troy Board of Education from July 1991 through June 2007 -- 16 years, several as president; a copy goes to Mrs. Sharon Spagnola and the official minutes. Signature lines list Nancy Philippart, President; Ida Edmunds, Vice President; Paula Fleming, Secretary; and trustees Gary Hauff, M'Liz Malven, Todd Miletti and Wendy Underwood.

CONSENT AGENDA -- AUGUST 16, 2011 MINUTES. Called to order at 7:24 p.m. by President Philippart following the Special Board Workshop, all seven members present with Superintendent Fowler and approximately 4 audience members. Resolution 11-081 (Hauff/Malven) approved minutes of June 21, 2011 and July 12, 2011, the Treasurer's Report for June and July 2011, and a diesel fuel bid award. Resolution 11-082 (Malven/Miletti) approved new hires Mark Chrzanowski, Chris Daugherty, Joseph Devault, Stephanie Donelko, Meghan Hall, Gary Koskinen, Lindsay Kuroski, Hannah Nagi, Natalie Selweski and Danielle Smit. Resolution 11-083 (Edmunds/Fleming) accepted applications under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979, as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, for ten non-resident 10th grade students for 2011-2012 attending the International Academy East program in Troy; resolution 11-084 (Miletti/Underwood) extended that option to an unlimited number of 9th grade students for 2012-2013. Resolution 11-085 (Fleming/Edmunds) cast the board's ballot for Donald Hubler, Region 8, three-year term, on the 2011 MASB Board of Directors. All votes were 7 ayes, 0 nays; adjourned 7:44 p.m., minutes by Secretary Paula Fleming.

PERSONNEL. Probationary contracts recommended for 2011-2012: Sara Ballinger (.9 FTE school psychologist), Julie Eldridge (5th grade, Costello), Ashley Falzon (4th grade, Troy Union), Eric Flessa (English/social studies, Athens), Lisa Gaglio (.68 FTE life skills, Baker Middle School), Amanda Hazergian (.5 FTE kindergarten, Barnard), Emily Louks (2nd grade, Costello), Melven Moffett (5th grade, Wattles), Jeanine Pica (resource room, Troy Union), Christopher Rich (psychology/social studies, Troy High), Cheryl Rowley (.5 FTE kindergarten, Hamilton) and Rita Suleyman (English, Athens); unmarked positions are 1.0 FTE.

SUMMER LEARNING UPDATE. Presented by Bob Stromayer, Director of Continuing Education. Elementary offerings were Go Figure Art, Adventures in Learning (new location at Hamilton), Jump Start (new sites at Hamilton and Barnard), GRASP, Title I and ESL (K-7); a new Summer Success Academy for students entering 9th grade drew 90% participation with over 70% earning credit; high school ESL was in its 3rd year. Enrollment: Elementary Summer Learning 284; Title 1 (Morse and Wattles) 165; ESL 186; GRASP (Books) 675; Middle School Summer Learning 202; middle school ESL 22; Summer Success 49; High School Summer School 881 (ESL 52); Adult ESL 146; Preschool (TOTS) 29; Summer Sensation Camps 252.

SUPERINTENDENT'S ANNUAL REPORT, 2010-2011. Graduation rate was 99% for the Class of 2010 and 98% for the Class of 2011, with 96.5% and 95% attending college. AP enrollment was 2029 in 2009-2010 (55% of the student body) with 86% earning college credit, and 2052 in 2010-2011 (58% of the student body) with 84% earning college credit; dual enrollment was 24 and 32 students. Fall conference parent attendance was 99% and 99% elementary, 86% and 78% middle, 83% and 86% high school across 2009-10 and 2010-11. All teachers are highly qualified, 73% hold a master's degree or higher and 9 have earned a Ph.D. All schools made AYP and received "A" grades on the Education YES! Report Card except a subgroup at Larson Middle School, a subgroup at Athens High School, and NCHS graduation and proficiency targets; all schools are NCA accredited. More than 600 students and staff earned first-in-state or national honors, there were 42 National Merit Scholar semifinalists, the Class of 2011 earned more than $16 million in scholarships, and Troy High and Athens High ranked in the top 5% of high schools nationwide. Board honors included one of eight Visionary Leadership Awards, one of 11 Standard of Excellence Awards and Honor Board status.

ENROLLMENT. District lines show 5253 general education, 51 special education and 5304 total, with 218.0 and 24.33 in the rooms and average columns, a 2010-11 row of 5095 and 197.5 and a 2011-2012 row of 199.5. Class size limits are DK 26K+, kindergarten 26 half-day, 1st 28, 2nd 28, 3rd 29, 4th 29 and 5th 29. BUSINESS -- SERVICE CONSOLIDATION PLAN AGREEMENT. The resolution recites that MCL 388.1622f(1)(c) requires a district that did not enter an agreement with the Michigan Department of Education under former section 11d as in effect for 2010-2011 to enter an agreement to develop a service consolidation plan; that the district already implemented cost savings through cooperative purchasing and service consolidation initiatives; and that the intent is to fully qualify for the $100 per pupil incentive payment under MCL 388.1622f Best Practices Incentive Grants, in compliance with MDE Service Consolidation Guidance distributed June 30, 2011. Attachment A is the agreement between MDE and Troy School District, signed by the District Superintendent, Board of Education President and Superintendent of Public Instruction; MDE states it meets the initial criteria in MCL 388.1622f(1)(c), one of four practices necessary to receive 2011-2012 State School Aid Best Financial Practice Incentive Funds. An August 31, 2011 memorandum from Mark S. Rajter (248/823-4010) explains that Section 388.1622f of the 2011-12 School Aid Bill requires 4 of 5 criteria for a one-time $100 per pupil payment for fiscal year 2011-2012 only, with no funds appropriated later, and that it helps offset the $470 per pupil reduction all districts incurred for 2011-12. The original Section 11d guidance (MCL 388.1611d) required a resolution by February 1, 2010 for flexibility in applying the $165 per pupil reduction against an unprotected categorical other than Section 22b for 2009-2010; Troy did not enter such an agreement for 2009-10.

OTHER. A resolution certifies Mrs. Ida Edmunds, Mrs. Paula Fleming and Mr. Todd Miletti as delegates to the MASB 2011 Delegate Assembly on October 27, 2011, tied to the MASB Fall Conference in November. Board committee membership for 2011-2012 (revision dated 8-24-11) assigns Edmunds to the NCA District Team and, with Hauff, the Safety Committee; Miletti to the Diversity Council; Edmunds, Hauff and Underwood to the Curriculum Committee; Edmunds, Hauff and Malven to the Policy Committee; and Fleming, Miletti and Philippart to the Superintendent Evaluation Committee, plus liaison roles to the Oakland Schools' Legislative Committee (second Wednesday at 6:30 p.m.), the Troy Business and Education Roundtable (TBERT, last Thursday at 11:30 a.m.), the Troy Community Coalition and the Wellness Policy Committee.
